baseline: postput1010-nfsall.json's pair (six switches, no probe, ref 772429156c), read with coldread.py: A2' (no POSTED_PUT) cold start 1 38.1 / 36.9 ms, B2' (POSTED_PUT) 35.8 / 34.9; warm 33.7 / 33.8 against 33.6 / 33.6; post-GO 33.4 throughout; cold v2 59 / 61 % against 59 / 65 %. coldstart1010-depth.json's runs so far on this ref (six switches + HAKUX_PROBE_WAITS=1, depth 2 = A, depth 3 = B): A 1-1791697258-coldstart1010-3142274 cold 38.3, A 1-1791697260-coldstart1010-3142523 37.7, B 1-1791697260-coldstart1010-3142465 37.0 (B 1-1791697259-coldstart1010-3142391 void at the cold start: a boot press took 10.3 s on a host adb liveness failure); cold ms per frame blocked in the rotation fence wait A 3.01 / 2.84, B 1.06.
prediction: #433 HAKUX_SUBMIT_FRAMES=3 on top of HAKUX_POSTED_PUT=1, at NFS MW's cold race start, six-switch base, both arms with HAKUX_PROBE_WAITS=1. The two act on one wait from two sides. POSTED_PUT lets the guest's DMA_PUT store go through while the PFIFO thread holds pfifo.lock, so the guest stops waiting on the lock, whatever holds it (fence waits or parsing). Depth 3 shortens what the PFIFO thread does under the lock: its slot rotation waits on the command buffer two finishes back instead of one. With the store posted, the guest's wait is gone either way, so depth 3 helps only where the PFIFO thread's own lateness paces the frame (postput1010: the guest spent what the posted store saved idle, +3.0 ms cold, waiting on the PFIFO thread). Point estimate: cold start 1 A 35.6 +- 1.0 (POSTED_PUT's 35.35 plus the probe's cost), B 35.0 +- 1.0, B - A -0.6 (range +0.3 .. -1.8); warm countdown B - A -0.1 (range -0.3 .. +0.2); post-GO 0 +- 0.2; cold v2 share +5 points (range -5 .. +20); cold ms per frame blocked in rotation A ~2.5, B ~0.9 (B/A 0.35). Probabilities: K (B <= 34.5, or cold v2 B - A >= +15) ~30 %; C (B - A <= -0.5) ~50 %; W ~85 %; G ~85 %; M ~70 %. A pass of C says the two stack and the player configuration is both; C failing with M passing says the posted store already took what depth 3 gives the pace, and the choice between them is cost and risk, not speed.
